# Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one

Coordinate `EN-115-000-0020-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M2-C-PH-M-0434` | `PM-223.2` | status ACTIVE | original slug `Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one-September-23-2026` | date 2026-09-23 | derived from the openai/math preprint Self-dual-random-cluster-interfaces-below-one-September-23-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "For every fixed $`0\\lt q\\lt 1`$, we prove that the Dobrushin interface of the square-lattice random-cluster model at its self-dual parameter converges to chordal SLE<sub><i>κ</i></sub>, where $`\\kappa=4\\pi/\\arccos(-\\sqrt q/2)\\in(6,8)`$. The approximating domains are simple closed nearest-neighbor lattice polygons with distinct marked vertices, whose marked boundary parametrizations converge uniformly to those of a bounded smooth Jordan domain. Convergence holds along the full mesh sequence in the uniform metric on oriented curves modulo increasing reparametrization. The proof combines finite connection comparisons below one, localization in irregular tiled disks, and a boundary observable that determines the limiting Loewner driver.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> For every fixed $`0\lt q\lt 1`$, we prove that the Dobrushin interface of the square-lattice random-cluster model at its self-dual parameter converges to chordal SLE<sub><i>κ</i></sub>, where $`\kappa=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)\in(6,8)`$. The approximating domains are simple closed nearest-neighbor lattice polygons with distinct marked vertices, whose marked boundary parametrizations converge uniformly to those of a bounded smooth Jordan domain. Convergence holds along the full mesh sequence in the uniform metric on oriented curves modulo increasing reparametrization. The proof combines finite connection comparisons below one, localization in irregular tiled disks, and a boundary observable that determines the limiting Loewner driver.

- **theorem-1** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): For every fixed $q\in(0,1)$ and every marked domain approximation just specified, the laws of $\eta_\delta$ converge as $\delta\to0$ in the metric <a href="#eq:curve-metric" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:curve-metric">[eq:curve-metric]</a> to chordal $\operatorname{SLE}_\kappa(D;a,b)$, where $$\kappa=\frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)}.$$ The convergence holds along the full mesh sequence.
  - Explanation: The prescribed self-dual interface has the chordal conformal scaling limit along the full mesh sequence.
- **corollary-2** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-full-fk-range)): For this statement, fix $q\in(0,4)$ and put $$p(q)=\frac{\sqrt q}{1+\sqrt q}, \qquad \kappa(q)=\frac{4\pi}{\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)}.$$ Let $D$ be a bounded Jordan domain with smooth simple boundary and distinct boundary marks $a,b$. Take simple nearest-neighbor lattice polygon approximations $D_{\delta_n}$, with $\delta_n\downarrow0$ and the full closed-polygon graphs specified above, and take $a_{\delta_n},b_{\delta_n}$ to be distinct polygon vertices. Require counterclockwise parametrizations of $\partial D_{\delta_n}$ converging uniformly on $[0,1]$ to one of $\partial D$, all injective on $[0,1)$, with the marks $a_{\delta_n},b_{\delta_n}$ and $a,b$ at parameters $0,1/2$ respectively. Wire all vertices of the counterclockwise arc from $b_{\delta_n}$ to $a_{\delta_n}$, including its endpoints, leaving the other boundary vertices singleton. Sample <a href="#eq:finite-target-law" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-target-law">[eq:finite-target-law]</a> with this $q$ and $p=p(q)$, and declare wired-arc boundary edges open for drawing. Then the prescribed medial strand, oriented from $a_{\delta_n}$ to $b_{\delta_n}$, converges in law along the full mesh sequence to chordal $\operatorname{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}(D;a,b)$ in <a href="#eq:curve-metric" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:curve-metric">[eq:curve-metric]</a>. No uniformity in $q$ is asserted.
  - Explanation: The complementary interface result extends the smooth-domain convergence conclusion to the stated combined range, without parameter uniformity.
- **lemma-3** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-finite-conditioning)): Conditioning on any set of edge states gives the random-cluster law on the remaining graph with the identifications induced by the open conditioned edges and the original partition. Conditional on all other edge states, an edge of odds $v$ has opening probability either $v/(1+v)$ or $v/(q+v)$, according as its endpoints are already connected or not. Changing a bounded number of edge states or pairwise vertex identifications therefore has bounded positive weight cost when the affected odds stay in a fixed compact subset of $(0,\infty)$.
  - Explanation: Revealed edges induce contractions and deletions in the remaining random-cluster law; bounded local changes have bounded weight cost.
- **lemma-5** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-loop-law)): For any fixed planar cap completion, the weight of a switch state in the homogeneous medium is proportional to $d^{\ell}$, where $\ell$ is its number of completed loops and $d=\sqrt q$. The proportionality factor is independent of the switch state. Changing a bounded number of loose-port pairings has bounded positive weight cost for every fixed $d>0$.
  - Explanation: Planar completion converts switch-state weights to positive loop weights with a state-independent normalization.
- **lemma-6** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-finite-duality)): Complementary dual-open edges have odds $q/v_e$. In particular the homogeneous square medium with odds $d=\sqrt q$ is self-dual. Complementary boundary caps are understood on the same cut surface.
  - Explanation: Complementary planar edges transform their odds by the stated duality rule, fixing the homogeneous self-dual medium.
- **theorem-7** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-pressure)): There are coefficients $c_m\ge0$, indexed by the nonzero multiindices $m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{V}$, such that $$-\log F_H(x)=\sum_{m\ne0}c_m x^m, \qquad x^m=\prod_{i\in V}x_i^{m_i}. \label{pressure:series}$$ The series converges absolutely on a polydisk containing the closed unit polydisk in its interior. If $c_m>0$, the support $\{i:m_i>0\}$ is connected in $H$.
  - Explanation: The negative logarithm of the site polynomial has nonnegative coefficients supported on connected vertex sets and an absolutely convergent expansion.
- **lemma-9** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-adjacent-rayleigh)): In every finite FK graph with $0<q<1$, two distinct edges incident to a common vertex have nonpositive covariance of their opening indicators. In a plane graph the same conclusion holds for two distinct edges incident to a common face. Both statements remain valid after deleting or contracting any other edges.
  - Explanation: Nonpositive edge covariance holds for incident edges and for cofacial edges in a plane graph, including after other edge deletions or contractions.
- **lemma-10** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-pressure-network-monotonicity)): Let $a,o$ be vertices in a finite graph. Adding or strengthening an edge incident to $o$ does not decrease $\mathbb P(a\leftrightarrow o)$. The same holds in a plane graph if the added edge and an auxiliary connection test edge from $a$ to $o$ can be drawn cofacially in the graph containing both edges. In particular, adding vertices to a terminal by identification does not decrease its connection probability to another fixed terminal.* *For any three vertices $a,b,o$, $$\mathbb P(a\leftrightarrow o,\ b\leftrightarrow o) \ge \mathbb P(a\leftrightarrow o)\mathbb P(b\leftrightarrow o). \label{pressure:root-correlation}$$
  - Explanation: The stated root and cofacial edge changes preserve tested connection monotonicity and give positive correlation of connections to a common root.
- **lemma-11** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-rooted)): For $a\in V$, the numbers $$\mu_H^a(m)=\frac q u m_a c_m \label{pressure:rooted-law}$$ define a probability law on finite nonempty vertex multisets with connected support containing $a$. In the graph with hub links above, $$\mathbb P_{H+o}(a\not\leftrightarrow o) =\sum_m\mu_H^a(m)x^m. \label{pressure:rooted-nonconnection}$$ If $S\subseteq V$ is nonempty, let $H/S$ identify precisely the vertices of $S$, with no other new identifications. Then $$\mathbb P_{H/S}(a\leftrightarrow S) =\mu_H^a\{m:\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}(m)\cap S\ne\varnothing\}. \label{pressure:rooted-hit}$$ Here $S$ on the left denotes the collapsed vertex. Equivalently, adjoin a fresh hub with exactly one infinite-odds link from each site of $S$ and no other incident links. Any identifications already represented in $H$ are retained. Writing $k_S(A)$ for the number of open components meeting $S$, $$K_H(S):=\log\mathbb E_H t^{k_S} =\sum_{\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}(m)\cap S\ne\varnothing}c_m. \label{pressure:coverage}$$ In particular $K_H$ is a nonnegative coverage function, $K_H(\{a\})=\log t$, and $$K_H(S)+K_H(T)-K_H(S\cup T) =\sum_{\substack{\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}(m)\cap S\ne\varnothing\\ \mathop{\mathrm{supp}}(m)\cap T\ne\varnothing}}c_m\ge0. \label{pressure:double-coverage}$$
  - Explanation: Pressure coefficients define a rooted probability law whose support-hit events represent connections to a collapsed target and boundary coverage gains.
- **lemma-14** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-interlacing)): Suppose four electrodes occur in cyclic order $A,C,B,D$ on the boundary of one disk. With $g_H$ defined by <a href="#pressure:network-g" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="pressure:network-g">[pressure:network-g]</a>, $$g_H(A,C)\ge g_H(A,B)\,g_H(C,D). \label{pressure:interlacing}$$ The edge odds may be arbitrary nonnegative finite numbers. The disk embedding and electrode-access assumptions are imposed after any preexisting identifications. Apart from the two wires specified in each $g_H$, there are no further abstract ties between distinct vertices of this embedded graph. All path witnesses in the proof use edges of this represented graph $H$ before the electrode wires are added. If $H$ is a quotient of an earlier physical graph, the statement alone does not assert that those paths lift to physical paths in the earlier graph.
  - Explanation: Interlacing electrodes in a disk permit a product lower bound for tested network connections under the specified absence of extra ties.
- **corollary-17** (theorem, [source](#stmt-rect-interlacing-abutments)): Let $G$ be a finite ordinary graph embedded in a closed disk, with the edge odds of this section. Let the nonempty electrodes $A,C,B,D$ be carried, in that cyclic order, by four accessible nondegenerate closed boundary arcs. Their relative interiors are pairwise disjoint, and only consecutive arcs in this cyclic order may share an endpoint. Assume $$A\cap C=A\cap B=C\cap D=\varnothing.$$ At every shared boundary incidence, the full physical-edge fan lies on the disk side. In a slightly enlarged disk, choose distinct boundary points $s,s'$, exterior spokes from $A$ to $s$ and from $B$ to $s'$, and outward access arcs from every $C$ vertex to one of the two open components of the enlarged boundary minus $\{s,s'\}$ and from every $D$ vertex to the other. The spokes and access arcs can be chosen with interiors disjoint from the graph and from one another. They may meet only at a designated shared electrode endpoint, except that the $A$ spokes may meet at $s$ and the $B$ spokes at $s'$. Then <a href="#rect:interlacing" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="rect:interlacing">[rect:interlacing]</a> holds.
  - Explanation: The interlacing comparison remains valid when accessible consecutive electrode arcs abut at endpoints under the explicit fan and spoke conditions.
- **proposition-22** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-rectangle-rsw)): For every fixed $\Lambda\ge1$ there is $c_\Lambda=c_\Lambda(q)>0$ such that $$\inf_{\substack{n,w\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\\w\le\Lambda n}}g_x(w,n) \ge c_\Lambda. \label{rect:rsw}$$ The same holds after translation, lattice rotation, reflection, or translation to the shifted dual square lattice. All probabilities refer to separate full crossing electrodes with no other wires.
  - Explanation: Separately wired crossing electrodes in rectangles of bounded aspect ratio have a uniform positive connection bound.
- **corollary-25** (theorem, [source](#stmt-rect-one-sided-marginal)): Suppose that an exterior configuration meets a collar only along $S$ and induces there an arbitrary noncrossing partition $X$, while $W$ is free. If the collar’s pure probability $g_H(S,W)$ tends to zero, adding the full wire at $W$ changes the exterior marginal by a density tending uniformly to one.
  - Explanation: Vanishing pure collar connection makes a remote full wire asymptotically invisible to the exterior marginal.
- **proposition-29** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-sector-network)): For every fixed finite $k\geq1$, every lattice rotation or reflection of the construction, and every translate of its center to a lattice site, $$\label{sector:network-decay} \lim_{L\to\infty}\ \sup_{\substack{1\leq r<R\\R/r\geq L}} Q_k(r,R)=0.$$ This is a separately wired two-terminal network statement on the noncyclic disk sector.
  - Explanation: The separately wired radial network test decays uniformly as the radial ratio grows on a fixed noncyclic sector.
- **corollary-37** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-sector-power)): For each fixed finite integer $k\ge1$ there are constants $C<\infty$ and $\eta>0$, depending on $q,k$, such that for all integer $1\le r<R$, $$\label{sector:power-arm} b_k(r,R)\le C(r/R)^\eta.$$ The same upper bound holds for actual crossings under arbitrary separate inner and outer cap partitions, with no other ties. Their partition-function ratio in <a href="#sector:actual-cap-ratio" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="sector:actual-cap-ratio">[sector:actual-cap-ratio]</a> lies between $1-C(r/R)^\eta$ and $1$.
  - Explanation: Actual sector crossings decay at a power rate, uniformly under separate end caps with no other ties.
- **proposition-47** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-annular-density)): Fix an ordinary square annulus of nonzero macroscopic width, with inner and outer rim sets $A,E$. There are $C<\infty$ and a mesh threshold depending only on $q$ and this fixed geometry such that, below that threshold, every pair of separate noncrossing cap partitions $X,Y$ on the two rims satisfies $$\|I_H(X,Y)\|\le C. \label{sector:annular-I}$$ The four pressures in $H,H/X,H/Y,H/(X,Y)$ between the rim images are uniformly bounded as well.* *The same conclusions hold for a fixed ordinary rectilinear polygonal annulus between two disjoint simple boundary cuts with positive separation. Constants may depend on this geometry; each rim must have a positive-length flat patch, and the ordinary bulk between the cuts must be connected. In particular a fixed thin ordinary polygonal collar with these properties is allowed.* *After attaching arbitrary planar graphs separately beyond the two cuts, changing an allowed cap on one side changes the opposite-side edge marginal by a uniformly bounded density and reciprocal density. This is a bounded comparison, not a density tending to one.
  - Explanation: Opposite annular caps and attached exterior graphs admit bounded reciprocal marginal comparisons at fixed geometry.
- **theorem-54** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-pure-disk)): Uniformly over either color and all disks in Convention <a href="#disk:conventions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="disk:conventions">48</a>, $$\lim_{L\to\infty} \sup_{\substack{I\subset B(z,r),\ J\cap B(z,R)=\varnothing\\ R/(1+r)\ge L}} p(Q)=0.$$
  - Explanation: Pure connection tests decay uniformly in irregular tiled disks as radial separation grows.
- **theorem-56** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-actual-disk)): There are $c,C>0$, depending only on the fixed model, such that in the disks of Convention <a href="#disk:conventions" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="disk:conventions">48</a>, $$\mathbb P(\text{actual }I\text{-to-}J\text{ path}) \le C\left(\frac{1+r}{R}\right)^c.$$ The bound is uniform under any planar noncrossing partition on the two end intervals, including a joint partition across the ends, provided there are no other ties. Thus a joint end cap may identify slots of $I$ with slots of $J$, but it contains no longitudinal-flank slots outside those end intervals.
  - Explanation: Actual physical crossings obey a uniform power bound under planar end partitions, including joint end caps, with no other ties.
- **corollary-66** (theorem, [source](#stmt-disk-grouped-cylinder)): Let $\mathcal C$ be a finite tiled cylinder of circumference comparable to $n$, with finite positive FK cap graphs drawn planarly at its rims. Its bottom has a flat mixed-color boundary near a specified flip-gap vertex $s$, and a second marked bottom point $t$ at distance comparable to $n$. All tiles in the following charts are ordinary. Fix their shape and buffer constants first, then take $n/r$ sufficiently large and $r$ sufficiently large in tile units.* *There are finitely many endpoint boxes in the bulk near $s$, with distances from $s$, depths from the bottom, and mutual spacings between fixed positive multiples of $r$. Their radii are at most $\delta r$, where $\delta>0$ is fixed sufficiently small. Each box has a disjoint ordinary bulk-annular buffer, of fixed relative width, within the scale-$r$ half-disk. Choose $c_0>0$ and $C_0<\infty$ so that these buffers lie strictly between radii $c_0r$ and $C_0r$ about $s$, with fixed positive margins. Their complement in this gap contains the clear two-arm splice layout of Lemma <a href="#lem:relative-arm" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:relative-arm">65</a>.* *Choose fixed $0<c_1<c_2$ so that the $s$-centered half-disk of radius $c_2n$ is an injective flat cylinder chart. The half-sector collar between its tile-level cuts at $c_1n$ and $c_2n$ has a sufficiently large fixed ratio for Lemma <a href="#disk:initial-collars" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="disk:initial-collars">60</a>. The $t$ box, of radius at most $\delta n$, and the remote middle region lie outside the $c_2n$ chart with positive $n$-scale margins. The attached graphs at this chart and at every endpoint buffer satisfy Definition <a href="#disk:regular-collars" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="disk:regular-collars">59</a>, with a fixed bound on all named bank classes and its residual-cap condition. In particular the graph outside the $s$ chart attaches only at its outer radial cut and those named hubs. A regular bulk window before the $t$ box and the middle contains a joining tube and a cleared corridor winding once between two distinct tube positions, as in Proposition <a href="#prop:routing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:routing">61</a>. For each of two spaced flat openings on the $c_1n$ target cut, a cleared branch joins its outward ordinary neighborhood to the tube. The branch and winding buffers have fixed positive $n$-scale clearances from the conditioned regions and satisfy the permitted local-chart contract.* *Let $\mathcal D$ specify the edge states in the endpoint boxes, the $t$ box, and the remote middle; consider any feasible value of these data. Let $R_{\mathrm{arm}}$ be the intersection of a short actual gap arm from $s$ to radius $c_0r$ and a separate same-color actual radial traversal from radius $C_0r$ to radius $c_1n$, both in the flat half-disk chart. Their supports avoid all the endpoint buffers. Choose a finite positive FK reference cap law that agrees with the cylinder law on the graph, odds, and deterministic wall portions through radius $c_2n$, including the endpoint buffers, and whose exterior at that cut is permitted. Let $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$ be its full actual gap arm from $s$ to a fixed full cutoff of radius comparable to $n$ and strictly beyond $c_1n$, with a fixed buffer. Put $$p_{\mathrm{ref}}:=\mathbb P_{\mathrm{ref}}(A_{\mathrm{ref}}).$$ The cutoff separates $s$ from the outer continuation of the reference chart, so trimming gives $A_{\mathrm{ref}}\subseteq R_{\mathrm{arm}}$. Let $E$ require an actual arm from $s$ joined to a noncontractible actual cycle in the stated bulk window. There is $c>0$ such that $$\label{disk:grouped-cycle-lower} \mathbb P(E\mid\mathcal D) \ge c\mathbb P(R_{\mathrm{arm}}\mid\mathcal D) \ge c^2 p_{\mathrm{ref}}.$$ For $k$ mutually separated opposite-color marker-traversal requirements $B_1,\ldots,B_k$, with their full splice windows between radii $2C_0r$ and $c_1n/2$, one also has $$\label{disk:grouped-marker-upper} \mathbb P\left(R_{\mathrm{arm}}\cap \bigcap_{j=1}^k B_j\,\middle\|\,\mathcal D\right) \le C(1-c)^k\mathbb P(R_{\mathrm{arm}}\mid\mathcal D).$$ Here $C=1$ is possible when every listed marker has its full window; the constant permits omission of boundedly many end markers. The constants depend on the fixed buffer choices and reference cutoff, but not on $r,n,k$ or the values of $\mathcal D$.
  - Explanation: The permitted buffered cylinder layout supports a relative arm-to-cycle splice and a geometric penalty for opposite-color marker traversals.
- **proposition-69** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-passage-moments)): For every fixed buffered regular annulus or sector and every $B\ge0$, its passage count $X$ satisfies $$\label{angular:passage-moment} \mathbb E\!\left[e^{BX}\mid\text{exterior states}\right]\le C_B.$$ The estimate is uniform in scale, sufficiently fine mesh, and the compatible exterior states. It also holds for the fixed macroscopic diameter tests of Definition <a href="#angular:passage-packing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="angular:passage-packing">68</a>, for a fixed finite family of such tests, and for an inventory with the stated fixed domination by their packing counts.
  - Explanation: Raw passage packing counts have all fixed exponential moments uniformly under compatible exterior conditioning.
- **corollary-71** (theorem, [source](#stmt-angular-polynomial-costs)): Up to radii $O(n^C)$ in mesh units, every fixed positive nest weight and each of its fixed real powers has expectation between $n^{-A}/C'$ and $C'n^A$, for constants depending on the fixed weight and geometry. Changing a cutoff by a fixed factor changes its expectation by a bounded factor. Changing a permitted exterior completion beyond such a fixed buffer, while keeping the patch, buffer, and deterministic wall portions unchanged, does the same. For a fixed weight $W$, uniformly for $t$ in a fixed compact interval, $$\left\|\log\mathbb EW^{t+\varepsilon} -\log\mathbb EW^t\right\| \le C\|\varepsilon\|\log n+O(\|\varepsilon\|)$$ when $\varepsilon$ stays in a sufficiently small fixed interval.
  - Explanation: Positive nest weights and fixed powers have polynomial costs, stable under fixed cutoff and permitted exterior changes.
- **theorem-76** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-angular-transfer)): For every fixed $\lambda$ in <a href="#angular:parameters" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="angular:parameters">[angular:parameters]</a>, let $B_{\mathrm{out},k}$ and $B_{\mathrm{in},k}$ be finite products of $P_{\xi,k}$ and $P_{\zeta,k}$, respectively, at real arguments in $[-v,v]$. Suppose that each product contains at least $n\ge1$ rows at argument zero. Then $$\begin{aligned} \limsup_{k\to\infty}\sup_{x\in[-v,v]} \\|B_{\mathrm{out},k}N_k(x)B_{\mathrm{in},k}\\| &\le C n^{-1+\rho},\label{angular:sandwich-first}\\ \limsup_{k\to\infty}\sup_{x,y\in[-v,v]} \\|B_{\mathrm{out},k} \{N_k(x)-e^{\mathrm i\tau(x-y)}N_k(y)\}B_{\mathrm{in},k}\\| &\le C n^{-1-\rho}.\label{angular:sandwich-second} \end{aligned}$$ Immediately to either side of each $N_k$, one may insert an even number, bounded by a fixed $L$, of additional rows with the corresponding twist, at arbitrary real arguments in $[-v,v]$. The two terms in <a href="#angular:sandwich-second" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="angular:sandwich-second">[angular:sandwich-second]</a> may use different additional lists. The constant can then depend on $L$, as well as on $\lambda$, but not on $n$ or on the real arguments. Moreover, $$\label{angular:contraction} \limsup_{k\to\infty}\sup_{x\in[-v,v]} \\|P_{\zeta,k}(x)\\|\le1.$$ The limit superior is taken for each fixed finite setup: its row counts and any geometric parameters are fixed before $k\to\infty$.
  - Explanation: Normalized homogeneous row sandwiches have distinct amplitude and phase-cancelled decay rates after the fixed-setup circumference limit.
- **theorem-91** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-physical-transfer)): Fix an integer $n\ge1$ and, at a fixed mesh, a finite physical-layer setup as above. All layer counts and all inserted edge matrices are fixed before even $N\to\infty$. Let $B_{\mathrm{out},N}$ and $B_{\mathrm{in},N}$ be products of the corresponding $\xi$- and $\zeta$-twist rows in <a href="#physical:vacuum-rows" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="physical:vacuum-rows">[physical:vacuum-rows]</a>, each containing at least $n$ rows. Every row is at a physical angle $\pm\gamma_0$.* *For $x,y\in\{-\gamma_0,\gamma_0\}$, define either $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal D_N^{\mathrm{low}} &=E_{\mathrm{out},N}\widehat{\mathcal N}_N(x)E_{\mathrm{in},N}, \label{physical:physical-low-operator}\\ \mathcal D_N^{\mathrm{high}} &=E^x_{\mathrm{out},N}\widehat{\mathcal N}_N(x)E^x_{\mathrm{in},N} -e^{\mathrm i\tau(x-y)}E^y_{\mathrm{out},N}\widehat{\mathcal N}_N(y) E^y_{\mathrm{in},N}. \label{physical:physical-high-operator} \end{aligned}$$ Each $E$ is a separately even product of at most a fixed $L$ physical rows with the corresponding twist. The lists for the two high terms may differ, but the exterior networks in <a href="#physical:external-states" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="physical:external-states">[physical:external-states]</a> are common to them. Every row in these displays has its own divisor $\Lambda_N$. Set, for $a=\mathrm{low},\mathrm{high}$, $$\label{physical:averaged-scalar} \mathcal C_N^a=\frac1{\|\mathcal S_N\|}\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal S_N} \left\langle\psi_{\mathrm{out},\sigma,N}, B_{\mathrm{out},N}\mathcal D_N^a B_{\mathrm{in},N} \psi_{\mathrm{in},\sigma,N}\right\rangle_{G_N}.$$ Then $\mathcal C^a=\lim_{N\to\infty,\ N\ \mathrm{even}}\mathcal C_N^a$ and $R_{\mathrm{in}},R_{\mathrm{out}}$, the corresponding limits of <a href="#physical:external-states" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="physical:external-states">[physical:external-states]</a>, exist. They are the square-plane scalar coefficient and its finite nonnegative reflected vacuum ratios. They satisfy $$\begin{aligned} \|\mathcal C^{\mathrm{low}}\| &\le C_{\lambda,L}n^{-1+\rho} \sqrt{R_{\mathrm{out}}R_{\mathrm{in}}}, \label{physical:scalar-low}\\ \|\mathcal C^{\mathrm{high}}\| &\le C_{\lambda,L}n^{-1-\rho} \sqrt{R_{\mathrm{out}}R_{\mathrm{in}}}. \label{physical:scalar-high} \end{aligned}$$ The analogous fixed-diagram reflection across an ordinary tile-axis cut gives the plane Cauchy–Schwarz inequality with its two reflected ratios.
  - Explanation: Finite physical-layer sandwiches yield plane scalar coefficients controlled by reflected vacuum ratios and the corresponding damping rates.
- **theorem-94** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-charge-budget)): For any fixed finite list of charges satisfying $$a_j>0,\qquad (1+a_j)\lambda<\pi/2,\qquad \sum_j a_j=1,$$ for every $\eta>0$ there is $C_{\eta,\mathbf a}<\infty$ such that the local costs obey $$\label{physical:charge-budget} P+D_*+\sum_j\log\frac{F_-(a_j)}{F_+(a_j)} \le \eta\log n+C_{\eta,\mathbf a}.$$ The assertion is valid for either global wire designation, with the fixed buffered cutoff conventions just specified. Equivalently, the left side has the one-sided $o(\log n)$ allowance defined above.
  - Explanation: Admissible charges bound the combined flat and bulk logarithmic cost by an arbitrarily small logarithmic allowance.
- **theorem-103** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-normalized-residual)): Let $\sigma$ have opposite signs on the two colors, each of absolute value one. For every fixed interior $z$, $$\frac{\mathbb E_{\mu_{\rm in}} [R_*\sigma(\operatorname{col}(V(z)))D_{V(z)}(2/d)^{N(z)}]} {\mathbb E_{\mu_{\rm in}}U_z}\longrightarrow0. \label{obs:normalized-residual}$$
  - Explanation: Positive normalization forces cancellation of the signed diagonal residual at an interior probe.
- **theorem-106** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-holomorphic)): Every locally uniform subsequential limit of $h_n$ is holomorphic in the ordinary complex coordinate of $\Omega$.
  - Explanation: Every locally uniform observable limit is holomorphic in the ordinary complex coordinate.
- **theorem-108** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-fixed-polygon)): Fix $0<q<1$, a rational simple orthogonal polygon $\Omega$, and four distinct ideal side-interior marks $p,b,c,d_0$ in counterclockwise order. Choose $M$ clearing all wall coordinates. For $n\in M\mathbb N$, use the exact whole-tile graph of $\Omega$ at mesh $1/n$, with either global color designation and the flat marked gaps of the specified color-visit convention within $O(1/n)$ of the ideal marks. Use the open-cap and deterministic separate-wire laws defined above. Only the marked gaps are rounded in this auxiliary experiment; the polygon walls remain exact.* *Choose a conformal half-plane coordinate taking $(p,b,c,d_0)$ to $(0,\chi,1,\infty)$, where $0<\chi<1$. Then, along every sequence $n\to\infty$ in $M\mathbb N$, $$\mathbb P_{\rm open}(E_{\mathfrak A})\longrightarrow r(\chi):= \frac{\displaystyle\int_1^\infty u^{\rho-1}\|u-\chi\|^{\rho-1}\|u-1\|^{1-3\rho}\,\,\mathrm du} {\displaystyle\int_\chi^\infty u^{\rho-1}\|u-\chi\|^{\rho-1}\|u-1\|^{1-3\rho}\,\,\mathrm du}. \label{obs:crossing-formula}$$ Under deterministic separate $\mathfrak A$ wires, the actual crossing probability tends to $$\frac{r(\chi)}{r(\chi)+d(1-r(\chi))}. \label{obs:deterministic-probability}$$ Moreover $h_n$ converges locally uniformly to the conformal map of Proposition <a href="#prop:obs-boundary-map" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:obs-boundary-map">107</a> with $r=r(\chi)$. The open-cap function satisfies $r(1-\chi)=1-r(\chi)$. If $g$ denotes <a href="#obs:deterministic-probability" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="obs:deterministic-probability">[obs:deterministic-probability]</a>, the complementary separate-wire probability is $$\frac{1-r}{dr+1-r}=\frac{1-g}{1-(1-q)g}. \label{obs:complementary-probability}$$
  - Explanation: Exact compatible polygon meshes have the stated conformal integral crossing law, its deterministic-wire conversion, and complementary symmetry.
- **theorem-110** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-moving-crossing)): Let $T_n$ be tiled disks of the class in Theorem <a href="#thm:pure-disk" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:pure-disk">54</a>, with mesh tending to zero, thick normalizations, and a common bounded physical range. In one color wire separately all the slots of two disjoint boundary intervals $A_n,B_n$, and impose no other ties. Suppose the four interval endpoints converge in chart coordinates to four distinct points in their prescribed cyclic order. If $\chi$ is their ordered cross-ratio, then $$\mathbb P_{T_n}(A_n\leftrightarrow B_n)\longrightarrow g(\chi).$$ The statement holds for either color, including cut-triangle cells and repeated physical boundary locations with distinct incidences. Equivalently, the error is uniform over sequences with fixed thickness and fixed positive chart separation of the four endpoints.
  - Explanation: Separated terminal endpoints in thick normalized varying disks give a uniform conformal crossing limit.
- **theorem-116** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-c2)): For the sufficiently fine rounded Dobrushin interfaces of Lemma <a href="#chordal:drawing" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="chordal:drawing">113</a>, the conditional probability of crossing an avoidable quadrilateral tends uniformly to zero as its crossing modulus tends to infinity. Uniformity includes the mesh, every stopping time before completion, every compatible stopped history, and every such quadrilateral in the remaining prime-end domain.* *For a marked domain approximation of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a>, the interfaces, transported to a fixed marked disk, consequently satisfy Condition C2 of (Kemppainen and Smirnov 2017) [[KemppainenSmirnov2017](#ref-KemppainenSmirnov2017)]. They are jointly subsequentially compact as oriented curves modulo increasing reparametrization and through their half-plane driving functions on compact capacity intervals. Every joint limit is a continuous Loewner-generating curve with the limiting driver, is parametrizable by strictly increasing capacity until the target, and has no additional time-ordered excursions omitted by this description. The target is reached only at completion. Curve compactness also holds in the original physical coordinates.
  - Explanation: Uniform conditional unforced-crossing decay gives joint curve and driving-function compactness, retaining time-ordered traversal.
- **proposition-118** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-driver)): Every subsequential joint limit supplied by Theorem <a href="#thm:c2" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:c2">116</a> from a marked domain approximation of Theorem <a href="#thm:main" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main">1</a> has half-plane driving process $$W_t=\sqrt\kappa B_t,\qquad \kappa=\frac4{1-\rho}=\frac{4\pi}{\pi-\lambda},$$ where $B$ is standard Brownian motion in the natural driver filtration.
  - Explanation: The bounded observable martingales identify each joint-limit driver as the stated scaled Brownian motion.
- **corollary-122** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-finite-extraction-rates)): Assume the parameter range of Theorem <a href="#thm:physical-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:physical-transfer">91</a>. In the setup of Proposition <a href="#prop:finite-extraction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:finite-extraction">121</a>, suppose the two clear sides contain at least $n$ physical time steps. Require the external tensors to come from fixed finite physical-layer networks of Theorem <a href="#thm:physical-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:physical-transfer">91</a>. Fix the mesh, the routing, and all inserted data before taking the even circumference-to-infinity limit. Normalize each physical row by its own vacuum divisor as in <a href="#physical:vacuum-rows" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="physical:vacuum-rows">[physical:vacuum-rows]</a>. The resulting plane vacuum coefficient is bounded by $$C n^{-1+\rho}\\|\Psi_-\\|\\|\Psi_+\\| \quad\hbox{or}\quad C n^{-1-\rho}\\|\Psi_-\\|\\|\Psi_+\\|, \label{calc:extraction-rates}$$ for the low or high stencil, respectively. Here $\\|\Psi_\pm\\|^2$ denotes the corresponding nonnegative reflected plane vacuum ratio, which is finite, with its matching cut kernel from Theorem <a href="#thm:physical-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:physical-transfer">91</a>. The constant may depend on the fixed routing geometry. Ordinary tile-axis folds satisfy the corresponding plane Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.
  - Explanation: Finite extraction with physical exterior networks inherits the low and high plane bounds together with reflected external norms.
- **lemma-125** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-calc-word-purification)): Suppose a finite word initially has length $m_0$ and each marker label occurs once. Given an integer $R\ge1$ and $\eta>0$, finitely many folds of the form <a href="#calc:word-fold" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="calc:word-fold">[calc:word-fold]</a>, followed by finitely many whole-word end folds, have the following property. In each nonempty leaf choose a majority label. Count a marker cell as usable only if it has that label and its $R$ neighboring cells on each side exist and have the same label. For either original marker, the expected number of its unusable copies is less than $\eta$.
  - Explanation: Finitely many permitted folds produce majority-label neighborhoods with arbitrarily small expected unusable-marker count.
- **lemma-126** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-calc-median-extraction)): Suppose a finite diagram contains $k_0$ favorable insertion copies with distinct diagonal projections. At an extraction, form two formal children by doubling the retained copies on either side and assigning each child weight $1/2$, as in the reflected diagrams of Proposition <a href="#prop:finite-extraction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:finite-extraction">121</a>. For every $\delta>0$, a finite tree of extractions leaves expected favorable count below $\delta$. More precisely, depth $T$ leaves at most $k_0^2/T$. All counts refer to these formal half-weights; no norm bound is asserted by this counting lemma.
  - Explanation: A finite extraction tree reduces the expected remaining favorable count; the counting assertion carries no norm bound.

      "exact_statement": "Let $\\mathcal C$ be a finite tiled cylinder of circumference comparable to $n$, with finite positive FK cap graphs drawn planarly at its rims. Its bottom has a flat mixed-color boundary near a specified flip-gap vertex $s$, and a second marked bottom point $t$ at distance comparable to $n$. All tiles in the following charts are ordinary. Fix their shape and buffer constants first, then take $n/r$ sufficiently large and $r$ sufficiently large in tile units.*\n\n*There are finitely many endpoint boxes in the bulk near $s$, with distances from $s$, depths from the bottom, and mutual spacings between fixed positive multiples of $r$. Their radii are at most $\\delta r$, where $\\delta>0$ is fixed sufficiently small. Each box has a disjoint ordinary bulk-annular buffer, of fixed relative width, within the scale-$r$ half-disk. Choose $c_0>0$ and $C_0<\\infty$ so that these buffers lie strictly between radii $c_0r$ and $C_0r$ about $s$, with fixed positive margins. Their complement in this gap contains the clear two-arm splice layout of Lemma <a href=\"#lem:relative-arm\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:relative-arm\">65</a>.*\n\n*Choose fixed $0<c_1<c_2$ so that the $s$-centered half-disk of radius $c_2n$ is an injective flat cylinder chart. The half-sector collar between its tile-level cuts at $c_1n$ and $c_2n$ has a sufficiently large fixed ratio for Lemma <a href=\"#disk:initial-collars\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"disk:initial-collars\">60</a>. The $t$ box, of radius at most $\\delta n$, and the remote middle region lie outside the $c_2n$ chart with positive $n$-scale margins. The attached graphs at this chart and at every endpoint buffer satisfy Definition <a href=\"#disk:regular-collars\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"disk:regular-collars\">59</a>, with a fixed bound on all named bank classes and its residual-cap condition. In particular the graph outside the $s$ chart attaches only at its outer radial cut and those named hubs. A regular bulk window before the $t$ box and the middle contains a joining tube and a cleared corridor winding once between two distinct tube positions, as in Proposition <a href=\"#prop:routing\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:routing\">61</a>. For each of two spaced flat openings on the $c_1n$ target cut, a cleared branch joins its outward ordinary neighborhood to the tube. The branch and winding buffers have fixed positive $n$-scale clearances from the conditioned regions and satisfy the permitted local-chart contract.*\n\n\n\n*Let $\\mathcal D$ specify the edge states in the endpoint boxes, the $t$ box, and the remote middle; consider any feasible value of these data. Let $R_{\\mathrm{arm}}$ be the intersection of a short actual gap arm from $s$ to radius $c_0r$ and a separate same-color actual radial traversal from radius $C_0r$ to radius $c_1n$, both in the flat half-disk chart. Their supports avoid all the endpoint buffers. Choose a finite positive FK reference cap law that agrees with the cylinder law on the graph, odds, and deterministic wall portions through radius $c_2n$, including the endpoint buffers, and whose exterior at that cut is permitted. Let $A_{\\mathrm{ref}}$ be its full actual gap arm from $s$ to a fixed full cutoff of radius comparable to $n$ and strictly beyond $c_1n$, with a fixed buffer. Let $E$ require an actual arm from $s$ joined to a noncontractible actual cycle in the stated bulk window. There is $c>0$ such that $$\\label{disk:grouped-cycle-lower}\n \\mathbb P(E\\mid\\mathcal D)\n    \\ge c\\mathbb P(R_{\\mathrm{arm}}\\mid\\mathcal D)\n    \\ge c^2 p_{\\mathrm{ref}}.$$ For $k$ mutually separated opposite-color marker-traversal requirements $B_1,\\ldots,B_k$, with their full splice windows between radii $2C_0r$ and $c_1n/2$, one also has $$\\label{disk:grouped-marker-upper}\n \\mathbb P\\left(R_{\\mathrm{arm}}\\cap\n                  \\bigcap_{j=1}^k B_j\\,\\middle|\\,\\mathcal D\\right)\n \\le C(1-c)^k\\mathbb P(R_{\\mathrm{arm}}\\mid\\mathcal D).$$ Here $C=1$ is possible when every listed marker has its full window; the constant permits omission of boundedly many end markers. Every row is at a physical angle $\\pm\\gamma_0$.*\n\n*For $x,y\\in\\{-\\gamma_0,\\gamma_0\\}$, define either $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathcal D_N^{\\mathrm{low}}\n &=E_{\\mathrm{out},N}\\widehat{\\mathcal N}_N(x)E_{\\mathrm{in},N},\n \\label{physical:physical-low-operator}\\\\\n \\mathcal D_N^{\\mathrm{high}}\n &=E^x_{\\mathrm{out},N}\\widehat{\\mathcal N}_N(x)E^x_{\\mathrm{in},N}\n -e^{\\mathrm i\\tau(x-y)}E^y_{\\mathrm{out},N}\\widehat{\\mathcal N}_N(y)\n       E^y_{\\mathrm{in},N}.\n \\label{physical:physical-high-operator}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Each $E$ is a separately even product of at most a fixed $L$ physical rows with the corresponding twist.       "exact_statement": "Fix $0<q<1$, a rational simple orthogonal polygon $\\Omega$, and four distinct ideal side-interior marks $p,b,c,d_0$ in counterclockwise order. Choose $M$ clearing all wall coordinates. For $n\\in M\\mathbb N$, use the exact whole-tile graph of $\\Omega$ at mesh $1/n$, with either global color designation and the flat marked gaps of the specified color-visit convention within $O(1/n)$ of the ideal marks. Use the open-cap and deterministic separate-wire laws defined above. Only the marked gaps are rounded in this auxiliary experiment; the polygon walls remain exact.*\n\n\n\n\n*Choose a conformal half-plane coordinate taking $(p,b,c,d_0)$ to $(0,\\chi,1,\\infty)$, where $0<\\chi<1$. Then, along every sequence $n\\to\\infty$ in $M\\mathbb N$, $$\\mathbb P_{\\rm open}(E_{\\mathfrak A})\\longrightarrow\n r(\\chi):=\n \\frac{\\displaystyle\\int_1^\\infty\n    u^{\\rho-1}|u-\\chi|^{\\rho-1}|u-1|^{1-3\\rho}\\,\\,\\mathrm du}\n {\\displaystyle\\int_\\chi^\\infty\n    u^{\\rho-1}|u-\\chi|^{\\rho-1}|u-1|^{1-3\\rho}\\,\\,\\mathrm du}.\n \\label{obs:crossing-formula}$$ Under deterministic separate $\\mathfrak A$ wires, the actual crossing probability tends to $$\\frac{r(\\chi)}{r(\\chi)+d(1-r(\\chi))}.\n \\label{obs:deterministic-probability}$$ Moreover $h_n$ converges locally uniformly to the conformal map of Proposition <a href=\"#prop:obs-boundary-map\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"prop:obs-boundary-map\">107</a> with $r=r(\\chi)$. The open-cap function satisfies $r(1-\\chi)=1-r(\\chi)$. If $g$ denotes <a href=\"#obs:deterministic-probability\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"obs:deterministic-probability\">[obs:deterministic-probability]</a>, the complementary separate-wire probability is $$\\frac{1-r}{dr+1-r}=\\frac{1-g}{1-(1-q)g}.\n \\label{obs:complementary-probability}$$",

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Network connection** ([source](#stmt-def-actual-network)): A *network connection* is an open connection in the graph after the prescribed vertex identifications.
- **Actual connection** ([source](#stmt-def-actual-network)): An *actual connection* uses open physical edges and does not jump between distinct vertices in a boundary class.
- **Odds partition function** ([source](#eq:odds-partition)): For a finite graph $G=(V,E)$ with positive edge odds $v_e$, write $$\label{eq:odds-partition} Z_G(q,\mathbf v)=\sum_{A\subseteq E}q^{k(A)}\prod_{e\in A}v_e.$$
- **Boundary partition** ([source](#eq:odds-partition)): A boundary partition $\xi$ means the quotient graph obtained by identifying vertices in each class.
- **Oriented curve metric** ([source](#eq:curve-metric)): For continuous oriented curves $\alpha,\beta:[0,1]\to\mathbb C$, put $$\label{eq:curve-metric} d_{\mathrm{curv}}(\alpha,\beta) =\inf_{\phi,\psi}\sup_{t\in[0,1]} \|\alpha(\phi(t))-\beta(\psi(t))\|,$$ where $\phi,\psi$ range over increasing homeomorphisms of $[0,1]$, and identify curves at zero distance.
- **Site polynomial** ([source](#pressure:polynomial)): For a vertex set $C$, put $x_C=\prod_{a\in C}x_a$ and define $$F_H(x)=\mathbb E_0\prod_{C\text{ component of }(V,A)}(1-u x_C). \label{pressure:polynomial}$$
- **Disk observable and open-cap probability** ([source](#pm-h-111)): Define the observable and the open-cap connection probability by $$h_n(z)=\frac{\mathbb E_{\rm open}H_{V(z)}}{P_0G_0}, \qquad r_n=\mathbb P_{\rm open}(E_{\mathfrak A}). \label{obs:observable}$$
- **Regular radial collar** ([source](#stmt-disk-regular-collars)): A regular radial collar is a full tile annulus or a union of a bounded number of tile sectors separated by straight coordinate walls.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-theorem-1** [claim](#stmt-thm-main) / [proof](#pm-h-3): The prescribed self-dual interface has the chordal conformal scaling limit along the full mesh sequence. -> Below-one interface convergence
- **step-corollary-2** [claim](#stmt-cor-full-fk-range) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-full-fk-range): The complementary interface result extends the smooth-domain convergence conclusion to the stated combined range, without parameter uniformity. -> Combined finite-law parameter range
- **step-lemma-3** [claim](#stmt-lem-finite-conditioning) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-finite-conditioning): Revealed edges induce contractions and deletions in the remaining random-cluster law; bounded local changes have bounded weight cost. -> Finite conditioning and bounded local changes
- **step-lemma-5** [claim](#stmt-lem-loop-law) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-loop-law): Planar completion converts switch-state weights to positive loop weights with a state-independent normalization. -> Positive loop law
- **step-lemma-6** [claim](#stmt-lem-finite-duality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-finite-duality): Complementary planar edges transform their odds by the stated duality rule, fixing the homogeneous self-dual medium. -> Finite planar duality
- **step-theorem-7** [claim](#stmt-thm-pressure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-pressure): The negative logarithm of the site polynomial has nonnegative coefficients supported on connected vertex sets and an absolutely convergent expansion. -> Positive site pressure
- **step-lemma-9** [claim](#stmt-lem-adjacent-rayleigh) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-adjacent-rayleigh): Nonpositive edge covariance holds for incident edges and for cofacial edges in a plane graph, including after other edge deletions or contractions. -> Adjacent and cofacial Rayleigh inequalities
- **step-lemma-10** [claim](#stmt-pressure-network-monotonicity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-pressure-network-monotonicity): The stated root and cofacial edge changes preserve tested connection monotonicity and give positive correlation of connections to a common root. -> Monotonicity of tested network connections
- **step-lemma-11** [claim](#stmt-lem-rooted) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-rooted): Pressure coefficients define a rooted probability law whose support-hit events represent connections to a collapsed target and boundary coverage gains. -> Rooted coverage representation
- **step-lemma-14** [claim](#stmt-lem-interlacing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-interlacing): Interlacing electrodes in a disk permit a product lower bound for tested network connections under the specified absence of extra ties. -> Interlacing gluing
- **step-corollary-17** [claim](#stmt-rect-interlacing-abutments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rect-interlacing-abutments): The interlacing comparison remains valid when accessible consecutive electrode arcs abut at endpoints under the explicit fan and spoke conditions. -> Interlacing with endpoint abutments
- **step-proposition-22** [claim](#stmt-prop-rectangle-rsw) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-rectangle-rsw): Separately wired crossing electrodes in rectangles of bounded aspect ratio have a uniform positive connection bound. -> Rectangle RSW for separate electrodes
- **step-corollary-25** [claim](#stmt-rect-one-sided-marginal) / [proof](#proof-stmt-rect-one-sided-marginal): Vanishing pure collar connection makes a remote full wire asymptotically invisible to the exterior marginal. -> A marginal comparison
- **step-proposition-29** [claim](#stmt-prop-sector-network) / [proof](#sector:radial-setup): The separately wired radial network test decays uniformly as the radial ratio grows on a fixed noncyclic sector. -> Radial network decay
- **step-corollary-37** [claim](#stmt-cor-sector-power) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-sector-power): Actual sector crossings decay at a power rate, uniformly under separate end caps with no other ties. -> Power-law sector bound
- **step-proposition-47** [claim](#stmt-prop-annular-density) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-annular-density): Opposite annular caps and attached exterior graphs admit bounded reciprocal marginal comparisons at fixed geometry. -> Bounded annular cap densities
- **step-theorem-54** [claim](#stmt-thm-pure-disk) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-pure-disk): Pure connection tests decay uniformly in irregular tiled disks as radial separation grows. -> Pure irregular-disk decay
- **step-theorem-56** [claim](#stmt-thm-actual-disk) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-actual-disk): Actual physical crossings obey a uniform power bound under planar end partitions, including joint end caps, with no other ties. -> Actual irregular-disk decay with end caps
- **step-corollary-66** [claim](#stmt-disk-grouped-cylinder) / [proof](#proof-stmt-disk-grouped-cylinder): The permitted buffered cylinder layout supports a relative arm-to-cycle splice and a geometric penalty for opposite-color marker traversals. -> The grouped cylinder splice
- **step-proposition-69** [claim](#stmt-prop-passage-moments) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-passage-moments): Raw passage packing counts have all fixed exponential moments uniformly under compatible exterior conditioning. -> All exponential passage moments
- **step-corollary-71** [claim](#stmt-angular-polynomial-costs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-angular-polynomial-costs): Positive nest weights and fixed powers have polynomial costs, stable under fixed cutoff and permitted exterior changes. -> Polynomial costs and fixed cutoffs
- **step-theorem-76** [claim](#stmt-thm-angular-transfer) / [proof](#pm-h-89): Normalized homogeneous row sandwiches have distinct amplitude and phase-cancelled decay rates after the fixed-setup circumference limit. -> Homogeneous angular sandwich
- **step-theorem-91** [claim](#stmt-thm-physical-transfer) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-physical-transfer): Finite physical-layer sandwiches yield plane scalar coefficients controlled by reflected vacuum ratios and the corresponding damping rates. -> Physical scalar estimate
- **step-theorem-94** [claim](#stmt-thm-charge-budget) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-charge-budget): Admissible charges bound the combined flat and bulk logarithmic cost by an arbitrarily small logarithmic allowance. -> Charge budget
- **step-theorem-103** [claim](#stmt-thm-normalized-residual) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-normalized-residual): Positive normalization forces cancellation of the signed diagonal residual at an interior probe. -> Normalized diagonal cancellation
- **step-theorem-106** [claim](#stmt-thm-holomorphic) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-holomorphic): Every locally uniform observable limit is holomorphic in the ordinary complex coordinate. -> Holomorphicity of the disk observable
- **step-theorem-108** [claim](#stmt-thm-fixed-polygon) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-fixed-polygon): Exact compatible polygon meshes have the stated conformal integral crossing law, its deterministic-wire conversion, and complementary symmetry. -> The fixed rational polygon formula
- **step-theorem-110** [claim](#stmt-thm-moving-crossing) / [proof](#pm-h-132): Separated terminal endpoints in thick normalized varying disks give a uniform conformal crossing limit. -> Moving two-terminal crossing formula
- **step-theorem-116** [claim](#stmt-thm-c2) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-c2): Uniform conditional unforced-crossing decay gives joint curve and driving-function compactness, retaining time-ordered traversal. -> Uniform unforced-crossing estimate
- **step-proposition-118** [claim](#stmt-prop-driver) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-driver): The bounded observable martingales identify each joint-limit driver as the stated scaled Brownian motion. -> Identification of the driver
- **step-corollary-122** [claim](#stmt-cor-finite-extraction-rates) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-finite-extraction-rates): Finite extraction with physical exterior networks inherits the low and high plane bounds together with reflected external norms. -> Physical extraction rates
- **step-lemma-125** [claim](#stmt-calc-word-purification) / [proof](#proof-stmt-calc-word-purification): Finitely many permitted folds produce majority-label neighborhoods with arbitrarily small expected unusable-marker count. -> Finite word purification
- **step-lemma-126** [claim](#stmt-lem-calc-median-extraction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-calc-median-extraction): A finite extraction tree reduces the expected remaining favorable count; the counting assertion carries no norm bound. -> Finite median extraction

<a id="pm-s4"></a>
## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **finite-conditioning**: Revealed edge states induce a conditional random-cluster law through open-edge contractions and closed-edge deletions. The conditional opening probability distinguishes endpoints already connected in the quotient from disconnected endpoints.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **arbitrary-association**: Promote tested connection comparisons to arbitrary increasing-event inequalities. -> The restricted comparisons provide no such general association or wiring monotonicity.
- **physical-shortcut**: Treat every quotient connection as a physical path. -> Boundary identifications can connect distinct physical vertices without an open physical route.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `constructive`. The finite conditioning lemma supplies exact conditional edge probabilities from finite graph connectivity. This executable specialization covers that finite identity; the interface scaling limit requires the separate analytic and geometric argument.

```python
# INPUTS: JSON list of finite graph cases with n, edges, odds, q, blocks, target, states.
# PRECONDITIONS: 1 <= n <= 3; at most 4 edges; positive rational q < 1 and odds; valid indices; target state is null.
# OUTPUTS: JSON list of reduced rational conditional opening probabilities.
# TIME: O(cases * (n + edges + total block size) * n), excluding rational bit cost.
# SPACE: O(n + cases), excluding input and rational bit storage.
# ARITHMETIC: exact python-flint fmpq arithmetic.
# FAILURE: malformed or out-of-contract input raises an exception; no approximate answer.
import json,sys
from flint import fmpq

def solve(c):
    n=c['n']; edges=c['edges']; states=c['states']; j=c['target']
    assert 1 <= n <= 3 and 1 <= len(edges) <= 4
    assert len(states)==len(edges) and 0 <= j < len(edges) and states[j] is None
    q=fmpq(c['q']); odds=[fmpq(v) for v in c['odds']]
    assert 0 < q < 1 and len(odds)==len(edges) and all(v>0 for v in odds)
    assert all(len(e)==2 and all(type(x) is int and 0<=x<n for x in e) for e in edges)
    assert all(s in (0,1) for k,s in enumerate(states) if k!=j)
    parent=list(range(n))
    def root(x):
        while parent[x]!=x: x=parent[x]
        return x
    def join(a,b): parent[root(a)]=root(b)
    seen=set()
    for block in c['blocks']:
        assert block and all(type(x) is int and 0<=x<n and x not in seen for x in block)
        assert len(set(block))==len(block)
        seen.update(block)
        for x in block[1:]: join(block[0],x)
    for k,(a,b) in enumerate(edges):
        if k!=j and states[k]==1: join(a,b)
    a,b=edges[j]; v=odds[j]
    denominator = 1 if root(a)==root(b) else q
    return str(v/(v+denominator))
print(json.dumps([solve(c) for c in json.load(sys.stdin)],separators=(',',':')))
```

    "reference_code": "# INPUTS: JSON list of finite graph cases with n, edges, odds, q, blocks, target, states.\n# PRECONDITIONS: 1 <= n <= 3; at most 4 edges; positive rational q < 1 and odds; valid indices; target state is null.\n# OUTPUTS: JSON list of reduced rational conditional opening probabilities.\n# TIME: O(cases * (n + edges + total block size) * n), excluding rational bit cost.\n# SPACE: O(n + cases), excluding input and rational bit storage.\n# ARITHMETIC: exact python-flint fmpq arithmetic.\n# FAILURE: malformed or out-of-contract input raises an exception; no approximate answer.\nimport json,sys\nfrom flint import fmpq\n\ndef solve(c):\n    n=c['n']; edges=c['edges']; states=c['states']; j=c['target']\n    assert 1 <= n <= 3 and 1 <= len(edges) <= 4\n    assert len(states)==len(edges) and 0 <= j < len(edges) and states[j] is None\n    q=fmpq(c['q']); odds=[fmpq(v) for v in c['odds']]\n    assert 0 < q < 1 and len(odds)==len(edges) and all(v>0 for v in odds)\n    assert all(len(e)==2 and all(type(x) is int and 0<=x<n for x in e) for e in edges)\n    assert all(s in (0,1) for k,s in enumerate(states) if k!=j)\n    parent=list(range(n))\n    def root(x):\n        while parent[x]!=x: x=parent[x]\n        return x\n    def join(a,b): parent[root(a)]=root(b)\n    seen=set()\n    for block in c['blocks']:\n        assert block and all(type(x) is int and 0<=x<n and x not in seen for x in block)\n        assert len(set(block))==len(block)\n        seen.update(block)\n        for x in block[1:]: join(block[0],x)\n    for k,(a,b) in enumerate(edges):\n        if k!=j and states[k]==1: join(a,b)\n    a,b=edges[j]; v=odds[j]\n    denominator = 1 if root(a)==root(b) else q\n    return str(v/(v+denominator))\nprint(json.dumps([solve(c) for c in json.load(sys.stdin)],separators=(',',':')))\n",

## 5. Domain engineering contracts

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | Finite random-cluster probability software can use the stated partition function and conditioning rules as a mathematical contract. A software implementation and its performance guarantees are ABSENT. |
| games_simulation | True | weak | adaptable | inferred | A simulator of the specified random-cluster lattice interface can compare its finite conditional probabilities and intended limiting law with the paper. A finite-mesh accuracy guarantee, mixing bound, and game mechanic are ABSENT. |
| tools | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | A finite probability checking tool can test normalization, conditioning, and adjacent-edge covariance against the paper. This supplies model-specific checks; an implementation is ABSENT. |
| algorithms | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | The finite configuration sum and conditional edge rule can be adapted to an exact small-graph reference calculation. The source does not provide an efficient general sampling algorithm or a runtime bound. |
| data_structures | True | moderate | adaptable | inferred | The rooted separator tree and ordered path products support a specialized representation of the finite observable. Its boundary-arc factor must remain distinct from the full string contribution of internal loops. |
| hardware_accelerators | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Finite transfer and graph formulas alone do not specify an accelerator architecture, memory layout, or hardware resource contract. Such a transfer is ABSENT. |
| crypto_security | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The random-cluster law and its correlation comparisons supply no cryptographic primitive, adversarial security model, or security reduction. A security contract is ABSENT. |
| machine_learning | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The source studies a specified finite probability law and its interface limit. A learning objective, training procedure, or generalization guarantee is ABSENT. |
| optimisation_operations_research | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Tested connection monotonicity and finite partition functions do not supply an optimization objective, feasible-set algorithm, or approximation guarantee. An operations-research contract is ABSENT. |
| distributed_systems | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | Graph boundary identifications encode a probability model; they do not specify processes, messages, failures, or a distributed consistency guarantee. A distributed implementation contract is ABSENT. |
| other (Planar random-cluster statistical physics) | True | strong | adaptable | stated | The paper directly supplies finite random-cluster identities and a scaling-limit theorem for the specified planar interface model. These support mathematical statistical-physics analysis under their stated hypotheses. |

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **L1** (hypothesis): The primary interface convergence theorem fixes the cluster weight in the below-one range and uses the self-dual square-lattice law. Blocked use: ['Applying the primary theorem to off-self-dual edge probabilities.', 'Treating the primary theorem alone as a result for arbitrary cluster weights.']
- **L2** (approximation): The initial marked approximation uses simple lattice polygons converging to a bounded Jordan domain with smooth simple boundary; its exclusion of slits and pinches concerns this initial approximation class. Blocked use: ['Replacing the initial approximation class by slit or pinched polygon boundaries.', 'Placing initial marks in lattice-edge interiors.', 'Extending the initial exclusion to every auxiliary tiled disk used later in the proof.']
- **L3** (hypothesis): The finite interface law wires one chosen boundary arc, includes its endpoints, and leaves the remaining boundary vertices singleton. Blocked use: ['Changing to arbitrary boundary partitions while retaining the same interface convergence conclusion.']
- **L4** (edge_case): The combined parameter-range corollary asserts no uniformity in the cluster weight. Blocked use: ['Taking parameter-dependent mesh limits as if convergence were uniform in the cluster weight.', 'Reading endpoint parameter limits into the fixed-parameter corollary.']
- **L5** (counterexample_scope): The comparison inequalities are restricted to tested connections and specified cofacial changes; they do not establish arbitrary-event positive association or arbitrary-wiring stochastic monotonicity. Blocked use: ['Using positive association for arbitrary increasing events.', 'Gluing overlapping rectangles by assuming arbitrary-boundary crossing comparisons.']
- **L6** (hypothesis): The boundary density comparisons require separate accessible end arcs, and the end-cap comparisons start without obstructing preexisting ties. Blocked use: ['Comparing arbitrary partitions on noncofacial rims.', 'Applying separate-end comparisons despite obstructing preexisting ties.']
- **L7** (hypothesis): Planar cap classes must admit noncrossing exterior connections; allowance for through hubs requires residual caps to remain separately planar. Blocked use: ['Substituting arbitrary crossing boundary partitions.', 'Using through hubs without the residual planarity condition.']
- **L8** (edge_case): Network connectivity can use boundary identifications that an actual physical path cannot use; extra boundary wires can destroy their equivalence. Blocked use: ['Reporting a quotient connection as a physical crossing without removing boundary shortcuts.']
- **L9** (approximation): Transfer limits hold with the finite insertion diagram fixed before later mesh or insertion limits. Blocked use: ['Exchanging circumference and mesh limits without a separate uniform estimate.', 'Treating bounded multiplicative comparisons as relative errors tending to zero.']
- **L10** (approximation): The auxiliary rational-polygon formula keeps polygon walls exact on compatible whole-tile meshes and rounds only the marked gaps. Blocked use: ['Applying the fixed-polygon formula directly to independently rounded wall families.']
- **L11** (counterexample_scope): The median extraction lemma controls formal expected counts under half-weights and does not itself bound norms. Blocked use: ['Replacing the operator estimates by the formal counting lemma alone.']
- **L12** (approximation): The curve metric retains orientation and traversal order and is stronger than convergence of traced sets or filled hulls. Blocked use: ['Replacing the claimed curve convergence by traced-set or filled-hull convergence alone.', 'Interpreting the curve topology as a prescribed time parametrization.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


For every fixed $`0\lt q\lt 1`$, we prove that the Dobrushin interface of the square-lattice random-cluster model at its self-dual parameter converges to chordal SLE<sub><i>κ</i></sub>, where $`\kappa=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)\in(6,8)`$. The approximating domains are simple closed nearest-neighbor lattice polygons with distinct marked vertices, whose marked boundary parametrizations converge uniformly to those of a bounded smooth Jordan domain. Convergence holds along the full mesh sequence in the uniform metric on oriented curves modulo increasing reparametrization. The proof combines finite connection comparisons below one, localization in irregular tiled disks, and a boundary observable that determines the limiting Loewner driver.
